utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber wants to use the first session for going through the MFI list. I take it that the parties have properly prepared for any submissions to be made. Before we do this, however, I'd like to put on the record that the Prosecution has communicated informally to the Chamber that no protective measures will be needed for 92 bis witnesses, Junjga Dragutin and Stevan Zaric. One could say that that goes without saying because there was no application within seven days. However, there was a limited application not within the seven days, which creates a risk to redact the address of the other witness, the other 92 bis witness, dealt with in the 3rd of November, 2008, decision. I think that message or that request came only on the 15th of December, which is six weeks after.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's right Your Honour. It was an oversight and we apologise and the Chamber staff communicated with us, and we checked and it is for Witness 65 which is seek to have the address redacted into 92 bis at the station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apologies should be addressed to the witness involved. Then we move on. And the first item on the list is, I think, D398.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, this is one that is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is one under seal, yes, it's.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Should we go into private session to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps out of an abundance of caution we might deal with it -- but I think it is preferable go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. D427 was a translation issue, and as far as the Chamber sees at this moment, nothing opposes D427 to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour the translation has been completed and revised document is released and attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then D427 in the absence of any observations is admitted into evidence. The next one is a document under seal, D563. The unredacted version still under seal has been uploaded by now and nothing opposes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The very same situation as with the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D563 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Under the seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal, yes. Then the next one is D568. The Chamber is drafting in relation to this document a written decision, and it has full priority for the Chamber. Next one is D720 on our list. We first have to point at a mistake in transcript page 7427, line 25, reference is made to D327 and that was a clear mistake. It was intended that a reference would be made to D720. That is now on the record. Then the Chamber will admit and does admit into evidence D720. We move on to the next one, is D725.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The Prosecution has advise the Defence via e-mail that we do not object to the admission of the relevant portions of D725.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand there are no further objections now and the parties have reached agreement on admission, and, therefore, D725 can be admitted and is admitted into evidence. We move on to D778. There are no further objections. Therefore, D778 is admitted into evidence. We move on to D792, a video footage. We do understand that the footage now uploaded is 30 minutes, 48 seconds, and that there's no objection against admission, and it's uploaded in e-court. Therefore, D792 is admitted into evidence. We move on to D829. This was a video uploaded of approximately 15 minutes, of which two minutes are played, the area between 6 minutes, 7 minutes, in which I think the witness was asked whether he recognised the area shown on this footage. There was an issue as to whether other parts should be played as well. Is there any further need to have other parts of the video played or reviewed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I don't think there is any need from the Defence side. Therefore, D829 in its entirety the 15 minutes, only which is played partly in court is admitted into evidence. We move to D831. That was, among other matters, also a translation issue. We do understand that the translation has now been uploaded and that therefore nothing opposes admission anymore. Therefore, D831 is admitted into evidence. The next one is D843. That is, if I could say the one judgement or two-judgement issue where the Chamber was quite a bit confused, and the Chamber wonders whether since Mr. Zganjer has now testified, whether there is any agreement among the parties, as the Chamber invited them to reach. That was --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe the issue was there was an excerpt of a judgement and the Chamber asked parties to upload the full judgement and I think it has been done under D843. We have the full judgement. So therefore I think there's nothing anymore that opposes admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So D84 being the judgement in its entirety is tendered, no objections and is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You said D84, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D843, yes, I'm sorry. D843. The full judgement, is admitted into evidence. For the next one, I think the Chamber indicated that we might need -- let's go into private session anyhow at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We were discussing D918 and P1063. The Prosecution does not oppose the admission of D918 and the Defence does not oppose the admission of P1063 so that the Chamber can determine how to interpret these two different versions of what is -- in many respects, the same document. D918 and P1063 are admitted into evidence. We move on to D954. I do understand that the correct B/C/S version of this document has been uploaded, which was, up till now, an obstacle to admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Actually my recollection Mr. President is slightly different and it was a longer article, and Mr. Mikulicic and I agreed to have only three pages, the relevant three pages replace that article and that has been done. So there is no longer any objections to D954.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is one little issue. And that is the original portion of this document that has been released under 3D01-0620, which is corresponds with an English version of the document. So the original should be attached to the English version of the documents and, therefore, the entire 954 should be replaced with a new translation of only three pages in English and two pages in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There was an issue about the original B/C/S -- the B/C/S original lacking, that was the reason that it was not admitted, and it was also unclear whether the entire exhibit was sought to be admitted or only a part of it. All this has not been settled, from what I understand. The B/C/S original is uploaded, and the relevant portions are there in translation. Therefore, Mr. Registrar, I take it that the references given by Mr. Mikulicic are sufficiently clear for you, and under those circumstances, D954, being an article titled: "The Confession of the Chetnik duke, Rade Cubrilo," 20th of March, 1996, is admitted into evidence in its relevant portions. We move on to D1079.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can assist the Chamber to expedite the matter. These were the following documents were all documents submitted to the bar table from the Defence in connection with Mr. Theunens' testimony, and the Prosecution does not object to any of them, so it's D1079, D1083, and then D1106, up to and including D1199.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a far longer list. Let's go through them one by one. The issue was - and I'm now returning to D1079 - first there was a problem with the unsourced last paragraph of this document provided by the assistant minister who authored this document. That was one problem. And the second one was that the Prosecution wished to examine the request by the Markac Defence, the request underlying the response. Now, I think, as a matter of fact, that the Chamber at that time expressed views on these last paragraphs - let me just find it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I could remind you, if I may, that it was Your Honours' wish to read the document in its entirety. And that's one issue. And the other issue was that the Prosecution office has requested to see the Markac Defence request to the Ministry of Justice, and we provided the Office of the Prosecutor with this request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, the Chamber said the following, and I'm referring to page 13528, where I said: "I leave it for the time being to the parties, whether the -- for -- whether the appropriate action to take would be, for example, to take out the last three lines that deals with facts and have a" -- and then have as a result a redacted version tendered into evidence and admitted into evidence, "or whether the parties agree that at this moment no factual support for rather blunt factual statements are there so that the parties agree that the Chamber, on the basis of this alone, could ignore this information." It's just untested factual information. Now have the parties agreed on either to redact or do the parties agree that the Chamber, on the basis of what the -- I think Assistant Minister Rajcic that the Chamber could not establish anything on the basis of that alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't think we have, but we'll talk with Mr. Mikulicic, and we will resolve the issue and inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's fine with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then the issue of the request to be shown to the Prosecution that has been resolved; but the other matter has not been resolved. Then we move on to D1083. The issue there was whether there was a full translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... whether it has been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We are still waiting for the official translation, so ... it has been re-sent to the TTS for translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we can't finally deal with it at this moment. Then we move on to D1106. I think nothing at this moment opposes admission of a set of letters which were MFI'd at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Quite so, Your Honour, they are old faithful, so to speak. We've raised them a number of times and there's never, ever been an objection to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then D1106 is admitted into evidence. The next D1107, and following, going up to D1181; that is, a bar table submission by the Cermak Defence. On the 15th of December, exhibit numbers were assigned. It was on the basis of this that I just gave you the numbers. It was established that D -- no, let me just first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall I try and assist?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had the numbers D1107 up to D1181 ready for admission. Then we have D1182 and D1183 are duplicates and have been vacated by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then what remains is D1184 up to and including D1199.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's -- so, therefore, admitted into evidence are D1107 through to D1181, the last one included, and D1184 through to and including D1199.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on to D12 -- 12 is not a matter we'll deal with at this moment. We move on to D1223. I think D1223 was not yet admitted into evidence because the witness was given an opportunity to review the -- the supplemental information sheet. He reported in court that he did not find any inaccuracies, and for that reason nothing opposes admission. Therefore, D1223 is admitted into evidence. Next one, D1225. For this document, the Prosecution has asked additional time to consider possible objections. This was done during 12th of January. Any objections Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There are no objections and the same was true of D1227 and D1229. So for all those three of those, the Prosecution does not have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1225, D1227, and D1229 are admitted into evidence. We move on to D1231. There was an issue whether this was -- should have been a bar table document or not, because the witness could not say much about D1231. But the Chamber is not aware of any objections even if the witness could not say anything about it. It doesn't mean it automatically lacks relevance and probative value.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, my information and I don't know what had transpired in court, if the objection was preserved or not. But there was one problem with the document in itself, whether bar tabled or through the witness, is that it was shown to the witness whether he couldn't say anything about it -- about the date of the death and there's an inconsistency within the document on page 2 of the document, the date of death is reporting as being the 4th August and on the page 3 of the very same document the date of death is 8th of August and since that was the purpose for tendering it, I think there was an issue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record I don't think that goes to admissibility as first point but secondly the item that Mr. Hedaraly referred on the second page doesn't -- on page 3 doesn't say that there's second date of death. It says when did the event occur. And it is listed as 8/8. But in terms of what it explicitly says what is the date of death, that is on the first page and it says 8/4. Whatever the case may be, we can argue at trial or in closing argument about the probative value, but I don't think this issue effects admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I looked at that time last night, Your Honour, if I can just have a few seconds just to make sure that I remember correctly. If the -- if the date of death is the 4th of August, and then the incident that caused the death on the 8th of August. On its face there is a problem with the document, and I don't think it's a matter of weight. I think it's a matter much the reliability, the inherent reliability of the document; and it is of such a point especially if it is tendered for that very purpose to contest when death he occurred which is why it was tendered initially then I think the probative value is so low because of the inheritance inconsistency that it cannot be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, these are records that we received from the Office of the Prosecutor so I expect there is no issue about authenticity. There is no issue that this is the official record. I don't think there is any issue of admissibility here because there is certainly no prejudice to the Prosecution if the document is admitted. Again rather than spending time here arguing about the document itself, I will reserve and argue it later; but I do think this is more of an issue of argument rather than the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, I take that the position of the Defence is more or less let the Chamber struggle with this document but that you would not oppose admission, and, of course, if there is contradicting information in the document, be aware that it will be a struggle for the Chamber. Do you want us to engage in the struggle, or would you save us?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was objecting to save the Chamber the struggle, but if the struggle will be saved by letting it into evidence then we will withdraw our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1231 is admitted into evidence. Then we move on to D1236. Mr. Hedaraly, the Prosecution asked for time to review the original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. For D1236 and D1237 -- and we have received those and we are satisfied. There are no objection to those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1236 and D1237 are admitted into evidence. As far as D1265 is concerned which is the Netherlands army publication entitled, "Combat Operations," I think the issue was what to select from that document because it was a 103-page document. I think parts of it were already in evidence, if I'm not mistaken, but I'm not certain about that -- not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what would be the selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understand it, we have now rescanned only seven pages of this document, and they are located at 1D65-0520.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And those are what pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, we'll pull that up, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'm already addressing you, Mr. Hedaraly, one of the issues was that Mr. Russo would like to have a look on whether he would like to have more pages selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Obviously we're waiting to know which pages the Defence will select. Now we'll look, if there's anything else. My understanding is I don't think in this particular document there is anything. But if I can just get back to the Chamber just to be absolutely sure that that is the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid that we are keeping matters on our MFI list, there always is a possibility to extend the number of pages admitted now. May I take it that if the Prosecution wants more there will be no objection against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D1265 as it is uploaded now, that is, seven pages are admitted into evidence and the -- if the Prosecution wants to add more pages to the selected portion of this document, they should inform the Defence and the Chamber within the next 48 hours. Then we move to the Prosecution exhibits. We start with P480. There was an issue about the authenticity of P480. Has any -- has this been resolved in any way or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, pursuant to the Chamber's instruction we provided the RFA response to the Defence back in the summer, I believe; and the Chamber had given them one week and we hadn't heard anything. This was the leaflet that had been exhibited, the bar table attached to one of the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was on the 27th of August, I think, when a week was granted to the Gotovina Defence to look at when and how the Prosecution had received this document. We have not heard anything since then. I now understand that -- that week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Then P480 is admitted into evidence. I do note that earlier there was a date attached to this document, the 5th of August, 1995, upon inquiries with the Prosecution, it turned out that that date, for which the basis was entirely unclear, was an error and therefore does not appear anymore in the description of this document. Mr. Registrar, am I reflecting the present situation correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on to P482, the book, an excerpt of the book. We have an English translation of ten pages. The whole of the book in B/C/S is 159 pages. The parties were invited to agree on what portions of the book should be uploaded and should be sought to be admitted into evidence. On the 25th of November, the legal officer of this Chamber asked the OTP to give an update to the Chamber by the 26th of November. The -- no response was received on 26th of November; and, therefore, on the 28th of November, the parties were reminded in court to resolve the issue, and we have not received any further response from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have talked with the Defence and the issue was the translation whether to have the entire book translated or relevant portions. The Prosecution initially only tendered two chapters of the book. The Defence wanted to tender the whole book, and the Prosecution does not have any objection to the entire book coming into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I think we had a subsequent conversation and the Prosecution was going to let me know -- we -- the discussion was we didn't need the whole book. However, I think on the record, when this came up the Prosecution was going to upload the introduction by General Gotovina where I believe on the record I said it says something to the effect of events as depicted in the book are not necessarily as they were in reality and that was part of the introduction and OTP was going to upload that portion which I think was one or two paragraphs and in the discussion with Mr. Tieger and Ms. Gustafson in order to avoid having to having to upload the entire book, there was a discussion about whether OTP would stipulate that in the entire book there is no reference of anybody having done anything wrong, and they were going to get back to me on that. And that would avoid us having to upload the entire book. So with those elements in mind, we would have no objection to the admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I was not aware of this latest development but I will check with Mr. Tieger and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the reasons why the Chamber scheduled this housekeeping session at this moment is because any remaining issue we'd like to be resolved within -- before Friday at the end of the day. I think you would like to have a stipulation and then have no further objections to those portions uploaded at this moment, or would any additional part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just the introduction. I would also add, Mr. President, that CLSS has told us that they will not translate the entire book. That was an additional reason why we had the discussion with OTP about how we can avoid ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it now seems you are very close to resolution of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are invited to reach a conclusion by the end of tomorrow, close of business tomorrow, and then we can decide the matter. I then move on to P505. I think that was the issue that was MFI'd where you questioned the authenticity, I think the letter was introduced --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, let me remind you, if I may. There is a really long pending issue. There is the letter of supposedly the letter issued by Mr. Markac, but the letter was not signed, it was not stamped and which not provided with an official number; and, therefore, we corroborate our position through tendering the Exhibits 909 and 910, and this is a request from Markac Defence to the Ministry of Justice and a response received from the Ministry of Justice, which states that there was no records in the official books, log-books in the Ministry of Interior of that letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now there once was an indication that the Prosecution would tender this document again during the testimony of a future witness. I'm not fully aware of which witness that would be, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was -- it was discussed with Witness Zganjer, who considered this to be an authentic document that transcript reference 11499, line 13 to 11500, line 25 and the Chamber had stated that it would decide on admission on the following page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we'll do. We now have all the information we need to decide the admissibility issue. The Chamber will decide the matter. We move on to P703. On the 12th of November, the Chamber has asked -- has invited the parties to further consider the matter, and we'd like to know whether the Prosecution still presses for admission of P703. And for the Gotovina Defence, whether the objection is still upheld.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In fact, P703 is the same as P177 already admitted, so P703 can be vacated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can be vacated. P703 is vacated. Then we have a series of document, starting with P769, P770, P771. Yes. These are documents which we're waiting, more or less, for a decision which was finally filed on the 5th of December. These are the reports on the terrain clearance. That was the issue of documents that were presented on the list to be used during cross-examination but finally not used. The Chamber has decided this matter in the 5th of December, decision, and, therefore sees no reason, at this moment, that the objection would still stand, in view of the Chamber's decision against P769, P770 and P771. These are, therefore, admitted into evidence. P778, the Chamber invited the parties to agree on a redacted version of this document. The Chamber understands that an agreement has been reached, that the redacted document has been uploaded and is ready for admission. P778 is admitted into evidence. We move on to P821. The issue there was whether the transcribed portion of a handwritten document, whether there was -- whether it was correctly transcribed, the Prosecution would check that. On the 5th of November, information was sought whether it had been checked already, and then we were informed that we'd further hear from the Prosecution, but I think we have no final answer yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the transcriptions and the translations in one language because if the Chamber remembers this document was transcribed in Danish and in English, so the corrected transcription raised in court by the Defence as well as translations in one language in English and B/C/S have been done. They have been forwarded to the -- to the -- to the registry late last year and it's only a matter of, I think, uploading and linking them; and I think they were sent to the Defence as well to verify but if not we can do that as well. But the documents are ready to be attached, and the corrected versions are ready to be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The notebooks, has the Defence teams received the new version of P821 and are there any objections against this now revised transcript of the notebook?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we -- we're struggling to find when it was sent to us. I don't doubt that it was, but we can't find it so, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest the following then that: The Chamber will hear before tomorrow close of business whether there's still any outstanding. So we receive a report anyhow. If the report would be there are no further objections then it seems that the document is ready for being admitted. If there are any further objections or if there's any further time needed to review the revised transcript and translation, then we'd like to hear from you not later than tomorrow, close of business. Then ... one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a whole series of document, starting at P899 up to and including P917. I think these exhibits have -- there was a memo dated 23rd of September which covered these documents, and the Chamber would like to know whether there are any objections to these MFI'd exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no objection against these documents to be admitted into evidence. Then P899 up to and including P917 are admitted into evidence. Next one is P923, which is the matter at stake there is an similar one as the matter decided in the 5th of December, 2008 decision, and therefore, it appears that, on the basis of that decision, nothing opposes admission anymore. In the absence of any objections, P923 is admitted into evidence. I would like to leave the decision on P1050 and P1051 for a moment and move on to P1052, P1055, and P1056. The Chamber has almost finished a written decision on these documents, so a decision will follow if not this week, that would be then be for practical reasons, then certainly early next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I understand they were admitted. The reasons were to follow so perhaps we could just admitted them into evidence. On the 18th December, there was oral decision with reasons to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're right. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1113, P1114, P1115; that is, the expert report by Reynaud Theunens, the addendum to the expert report by Reynaud Theunens, and the corrigendum to the expert report by Reynaud Theunens, are admitted into evidence. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I misinformed you. utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, just for the sake of consistency when we discussed these first four witness interviews, I know we had --

utterances.text: Yes, it's P1052, P1055, P1056 and P1059, and I don't think they were formally admitted, but they are covered by that same decision with reasons to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are admitted into evidence all the numbers, the four numbers you just read. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.text: Yes. As well as for P1256, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And on the same assumption, P1255 is admitted into evidence. A similar issue arises with P1256 although slightly different because part of the photographs were already in evidence but an opportunity was given to further review the Knin exhumation photographic presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then P1256 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.text: We now move to P1257. Mr. Kehoe asked for time to review P1257.

utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection to the admission of the report. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then P1257 is admitted into evidence. Then we have P1259, P1260, P1261, P1262. P1273, the famous "stacionar" issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we have about half the Tribunal working on that word and have not been successful so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should engage the other half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will, Your Honour. We will. And if I may take the opportunity, Mr. President, I'm advised that with respect to D914, we have uploaded the additional two pages, pages 3 and 4, that OTP wanted uploaded, and it is now in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said D914. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Then as such, the even -- there were two issues in relation to P1273, the first one was the translation or the meaning of the word "stacionar" and the second was about the use of this map in Operation Storm. Does that go to admissibility in relation to relevance or ... Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess it would go -- the Court is the gate keeper of what evidence comes in. If it is not related to Operation Storm obviously we could put in various exhibits, and it might have some probative value but in terms of under 89 (D), the overall prejudice in terms of introducing matters that might be extremely tangential unless there's a link established connecting that document somehow to Operation Storm, we would argue that it shouldn't be admitted because it might then call for to us to have to move some evidence in about positions in 1993 which obviously the OTP's admitting it for some purpose. We would have to come up with evidence to meet that purpose and rather, in my view, spending time and resources on a training exercise map from 1993 where there is no evidence that it is connect to the operation, I would argue that it should not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe the argument was made on the record but I can repeat it, and the Prosecution's position is that it would be an issue of weight. It is relevant to the extent that even if it is a training map, there are targets that are listed there that on their face are not military targets. So in any event, they do raise an issue regarding intent which is obviously one of the issues in this case. So there is relevance to it, and there is enough relevance and probative value for it to be admissible. Of course, the weight of it will be less because it is a training map from 1993 but that does not bar admissibility of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you say on the face, you are primarily referring to the description of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just respond, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, under the protocol a structure is not on its face not a military target that. Depends on what that structure was being used for at the time, and whether something is a military target is depends on the use; if there is no evidence provided by the Prosecution stating even if their translation were ultimately to be used what that facility was actually being used for, it doesn't tell us anything about whether it was a legitimate military target or military objective or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There was also an issue raised by Mr. Konings whether the very fact that things without descriptions that could lead someone to believe that this -- not a military target without specifically describing why or what the purpose of it was, so in that sense it is also relevant in light of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber admits into evidence P1273 and waits for further follow-up, specifically in relation to the "stacionar" issue, after the other half of the Tribunal has expressed its views on it. Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number to this attachment, which is Appendix A to the joint submission? And I think it is uploaded under 65 ter number 5982.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P1282.

utterances.text: P1282 is admitted into evidence. The second map issue. In the last paragraph of this joint submission, the OTP has asked the -- for the map binder to be admitted. utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm advised by Mr. Kehoe that we have admitted some of these maps into evidence through the cross-examination of Mr. Konings, and I think we need to check to make sure that we're now not double counting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'd like to hear whether there is agreement on the whole of the map binder what to be -- to admit and was is standard and what is not standard and whether there are any objections. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we'll have to look at to what extent admission of the binder as such would result in any duplicates. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as the next witness to be called concerns , the Chamber has not had sufficient time to consider the details of the objections against the admission of exhibits attached to the statements. From I understand, the Cermak Defence had no objections whatsoever; the Gotovina Defence had objection against mainly against the exhibits attached rather than to the statements. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. It's the exhibits not the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then, Mr. Kuzmanovic, I haven't seen but it could be my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's been filed. I don't think it's been sent out by the service yet. Basically the bottom line for us is we don't object to the statements. The issue is with some of the exhibits either duplication or exhibits that were late, or -- basically along the same lines as the Gotovina Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question is whether we can proceed before having finally considered this matter. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There are several issues that I want to try to clarify. There's issues about admissibility as I understand because the Defence claims that the witness was not present at the time the reports were prepared. To me, that's an issue of weight or admissibility of the document at the time of admission not addition to the 65 ter list and for those documents where he was not, he will be asked questions regarding his knowledge of these events or sometimes patterns involved. So I think those are not really objections -- they are formally been objected to be added to the 65 ter list, but those all ultimately admissibility issues, and we think it is a weight issue. Then there are -- the other categories of document which are three formal attachments to the witness statement, and the Prosecution had indicated along time ago and the practice had been consistent that attachments to witness statements were part of the witness statement and although not formally sought to be added to the 65 ter list would be used at trial as evidence, most of our witnesses had attachments to their witness statements and then once again if the issues of admissibility we can deal with that as we proceed. But so from the Prosecution's point of view, the objections of the Defence are more admissibility objections than admission to things we had added to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say some of the issues raised in the objections will be dealt with during the examination of the witness. And as far as attachments being an inherent part of -- of statements, the statements including the references to those documents and these documents themselves were disclosed --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It is essentially a notice issue, Your Honour, that once they were notified of the witness statement the attachments are referred to it. So there is no notice aspect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. They are disclosed. The documents the witness refers to in his statement are disclosed well in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That that's not necessarily true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I was waiting for my learned friend to finish before I disagree with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, even -- there might even not be a need to disagree with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's hear what Mr. Hedaraly tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There was an issue in this case about the diary in the aerial photograph which apparently were not disclosed with the witness statement last year for some technical reason, but regardless, the witness statement in the second paragraph clearly said that the witness provides a diary. There are repeated mentions of the diary in the statement and we never heard from the Defence that those were not disclosed. It is only in preparing for the witness that I noticed that those attachments had not been formally disclosed, but they are referred in such a way in the statement that everyone is clearly notified. So that if the statements had been reviewed, we would have known that the -- there was a problem with disclosure. But they were disclosed I think on the 8th of January when I was preparing for -- for this witness, and I realised that there had been an inadvertent omission with respect to two attachments to the 2008 statement which was disclosed well in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You disagree, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I mean first I appreciate that counsel's onus to put the burden back on the Defence as opposed to taking the responsibility of the OTP which was to routinely disclose those exhibits that they are intending to put into evidence; and I assume that in reviewing their case they recognised some time ago that they hadn't disclosed this, and we only got notification of it in January. There does seem to be a pattern with this with the OTP. We can address that at a different time, but that is not the sole purpose of all of these -- our objections to these exhibits. Yes, some of them fall into disclosure and if we can just go down through them seriatim. C 1, of course, is the one that is in his statement, but if we look at what is C 2 and C 4, which are instructive, those are the diary of the witness and also a report for ECMM dated 15 September 1995. Now, this apparently was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor in April of 2008. And were not disclosed. So I mean, obviously, there is considerable delay in that regard. C 1, of course, is a newspaper article that he doesn't refer to in any way, shape, or form. The aerial photograph C 3, I mean that, of course, was not disclosed either. And then we have a series of documents -- well, actually there is a series of documents we're talking about D12 which is frankly so redacted. No one can understand exactly who is the source of that document. But then we have a series of documents from going from D6 through D17 which are ECMM reports -- excuse me D16, yes, D17 as well because it refers to the time-frame when he was -- he, Mr. Hansen was gone. He was gone from Sector South from 17 August to 5 September. Now, the difficulty with this, Your Honour, is: Number one, the Office of the Prosecutor had these ECMM reports; and number two, there were ECMM officials such as Mr. Liborius, such as Mr. Hendricks, such as others that were there during that operative time-frame, and for some reason, known only to the Office of the Prosecutor, they chose not to provide those witnesses with these document. I still don't understand that why -- understand why. Nevertheless they put these documents on a witness list with a witness who wasn't even present at the time, and I suspect based on what Mr. Hedaraly just said he expects to ask questions about information in those reports when the witness wasn't even there. That goes from -- if I can just check my notes, that goes from D6 through D17. We object, of course, to the redactions that are in D12. And, of course, we reject to it, the failure to disclose C 1, C 2, C 4, all of which were in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor no later than April of 2008. Likewise just based on the prior rulings of the Court C 1 is a newspaper article that this witness isn't quoted; this witness isn't referred to. I think it's a Globus article of 11 August 1995. So the objections pursuant to our motion fall into a variety of categories: Lack of disclosure, lack of timely disclosure, notwithstanding the Prosecution's attempt to put the onus on the Defence; the redaction, and the attempt to put any number of exhibits D6 through D17 in through a witness who wasn't there at the time when there were many other witnesses with which these documents could have been discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly -- yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interpreting. We just want to put our position the record, Your Honour. We just saw on the e-mail that our filing has been submitted everyone. There was one omission in the filing and that's related to C 1 meaning that we object to the argument -- or to the article as this particular witness has not -- was not mentioned in the article. He has nothing do with the article. And all of the other arguments that were put fort in our motion will stand by and are similar to the arguments that Mr. Kehoe's made, specifically regarding this particular witness not being present during certain portions of -- of these ECMM reports and many portions of these ECMM reports have information that is completely outside the scope of -- of matters in the indictment meaning talking about situations in other parts of the former Yugoslavia. Several of those documents have large sections devoted to that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now when we're talking about, Mr. Hedaraly, I will give you an opportunity to briefly respond. Now, as far as reports, including elements which deal with other parts of the former Yugoslavia, would have you any problem in redacting them to take them out. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think is a more a practical issue. Usually those sections are clearly delineated. I think we have seen some of the reports that usually overall reports from ECMM, higher, from Zagreb, for example, and there's a section that clearly says Croatia. It says Bosnia or Sector East. We can redact them but it seems that we can all agree that those are irrelevant and should not be paid any attention, and I am more than happy to stipulate those portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, would that, at least in respect of this element be would be a solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be fine, Your Honour. Just as an example, I can give you an example. 65 ter 7009, the last essentially four -- two to three pages have nothing to do with Sector South so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it seems that a proposed solution there could be reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be agreeable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hedaraly apart from this rather practical matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There's also -- there's a few issues that I tried -- I think I tried to untangle, and I'm not going to repeat myself. The report where it is came claims that Mr. Hansen was not there this is an issue of admissibility with the witness or alternatively a bar table issue but it's not an issue of addition to 65 ter list. That's the first point. With respect to the attachments and the disclosure issue, I did not try to put the onus on the Defence. I acknowledged that it was an error on the Prosecution's part. I was simply pointing out that the prejudice may not be as high as it is claimed here. Finally, the newspaper article has already been, a part of it, admitted into evidence under P701, which is Mr. Alun Roberts's testimony; and that was a globus article. Mr. Hansen attached a translation that he had received in 1995 and had it provided to the Office of the Prosecutor and attached to his statement; so we just are now using the full article and we got the original, as well, uploaded. And it is not true that it is not mentioned in any way, shape, or form in his first statement he does -- although he is not mentioned himself in the article, it is his position that he received that it is a contemporaneous newspaper article of the time of 11 August. So we're not talking about the 2000 or 1999 or 2006. We're talking about a contemporaneous report of what happened during Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If is he not mentioned in it, he's not quoted in it, he's got nothing to do with writing it, what is the relevance of going true it with him? I mean, it's an exercise again of going through documents with which the witness clearly has no applicability. Contrary, I mean, the Prosecution seems to think that any document that -- they bring before this Chamber can be admitted, and it's not a question of admissibility, it's a question of weight. There has to be some screen to this, and part of that screen is -- part of the screen that should be imposed on the Prosecution is in a document such as this. Now, the exercise -- I go back, and counsel has not answered that, the exercise of putting documents in that counsel maintains go to admissibility those documents -- when Mr. Hansen wasn't there, those documents should have been discussed with witnesses that were there. Not with somebody that was on leave someplace and certainly the underpinnings of those documents go to its admissibility and asking the rhetorical request: Why didn't the Prosecutor ask these questions to witnesses who were there when they would have written --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be more convenient to wait to see what questions I put to the witness before making those decisions, and frankly, I mean, I'm stunned by the fact that documents are being put that the witness knows nothing about concerning a number of exhibits numbers that the Defence has [Overlapping speakers] ... that's just shocking, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- I think we there's no need to spend further time on one party blaming another party that publications are tendered into evidence where the direct link with the witness is not always a full 100 percent clear. I think that happened on both sides, or should I say on four sides. The issue, that issue is clear to the Chamber and we struggle with it now and then. Any further submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but it obviously would affect the examination significantly. First of all, to know whether they are admitted to the 65 ter list; and, second of all, and whether the attachments will be objected to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber needs perhaps not hours but at least needs a bit of time to consider how to proceed. We'll adjourn but everyone should remain stand by.

utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I have a binder of hard copies of the documents on the exhibit list. If that can be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I first want to refer you to your first statement, which is at tab 1 of your binder, which is now P1283. And I want to focus at the bottom of the second page, the first page of text, where you stated: "Apart from ARSK headquarters staff there was never a military defence of Knin. Troops, artillery, and tanks were all deployed on the front lines and soldiers were only seen in Knin when on leave and [sic] rotating." I want to ask, explore this will you a little bit, and my first question for you is: Did you actually these ARSK troops, artillery, and tanks deployed on the front line?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Affirmative. When travelling across the -- the front line, we saw to some extent the deployment of RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what could you see in Knin itself, in terms of ARSK troops, artillery, and tanks?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Well, as I -- I highlight in the statement, we -- I don't recall seeing any manoeuvring of heavy materiel or heavy equipment; and it was, though, a regular mission to see uniformed personnel walking the streets of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, you announced in paragraph 2 of your submission, 92 ter submission that you would read a summary. Now for everyone to better understand the additional questions that will be answered by the witness, perhaps it would be a good idea to do it right in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you explained to Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have a summary. I just omitted to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen was an ECMM monitor in UN Sector South from June 1995 to September 1995. He was on the N2 monitoring team until the ECMM reorganisation in September 1995 when he became the leader of monitoring team K1. He personally observed the shelling of Knin on 4 August and witnessed shells falling in residential areas including in the immediate vicinity of his accommodation. In the first days after the offensive, he was able to observe HV soldiers storing and carrying away looted valuable items right in front of the UN compound. In the course of his monitoring activities, he witnessed various incidents of looting and burning, as well as cases of harassment and killings of local Serbs. Mr. Hansen had regular meetings with Accused Cermak, to whom ECMM would often report about the lack of law and order in the Sector and about restrictions of movement. He also met with Accused Gotovina on 20 September 1995 and confronted him with other members of ECMM with the widespread crimes of looting, arson, and harassment. This concludes my summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, going back to Knin, before Operation Storm, did you see any units or any organised groups of soldiers in the town?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you ever visit the northern barracks in Knin prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Affirmative. On a few occasions, we visited the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was the context of those visits or the purpose of those visits?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Well, liaison with -- with staff officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember when was your last visit before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't have any precise recollection of the dates of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you describe your observations on those occasions regarding the level of activity in the northern barracks on your visits there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I -- I saw a kind of a dull, lower activity situation, not really indicating a lot of activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And was that the same on each of your visits there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In your first statement, still staying with your first statement, on the paragraph immediately preceding the one we were just discussing, you talk about the Tvik factory and the railroad and their contribution to the economy. And I just want, first of all, to clarify that when you're referring to before the war, you mean before 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, did you ever, prior to Operation Storm, visit the Tvik factory in Knin?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I visited the factory on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber what was the purpose of those visits?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: At that time, we were conducting an economic survey of the pre-war economy in the entire region.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was, to your knowledge, the purpose of the Tvik factory? What was it producing?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: It was producing nuts and bolts to the -- to the Yugoslav market.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In your visits there is in June and July of 1995 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I object. That's not what he said. If he wants to ask the dates he was there, that's fine, not leading the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, you arrived in Knin on 29 May 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: An Operation Storm started on 4 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So your visits to the Tvik factory would be between 29 May 1995 and 4 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the course of your visits to the Tvik factory in 1995, before Operation Storm, was the Tvik factory working, was it producing anything?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: No. The production had ceased and staff there were basically maintaining or guarding assets at the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you have any conversations with anyone at the Tvik factory in that -- in those times?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: The dates of the visits I was in dialogue with a manager of Tvik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in the course of these discussions with the manager of the Tvik factory, did he ever tell you anything about converting the factory to produce --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, stop. I have to cease the leading. I mean, if we are going to talk about a conversation; number one, it is it hearsay, but at least ask what was said during the conversation and not testimony by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did he have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, a yes or no question, leading questions are very often yes or no questions; so, therefore, that answer as such -- but let me just re-read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I can go through all the topics --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The question leads to the extent that it directs the attention of the witness into a certain area. That could have been done in a more neutral way, and you're invited to rephrase your question. At the same time, Mr. Kehoe, I was a bit surprised by your previous objection which took Mr. Hedaraly quite a bit of time, the June, July issue. If it is in evidence that someone arrives in late May. And if it is prior to Operation Storm, of course, it could have been that he had been there three years ago as well. But would you not expect under those circumstances that the witness would immediately say, Of course, it was not there, it must have been at another occasion. And technically it might have been right whether it wasn't necessary to object against, that leading is highly questionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President if I could respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No. You're not going respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... there is an answer. When do take a break, Mr. President, I'd like to respond to that because there is a response because it goes directly to evidence that's already been presented to this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The witness was there. June, July, just talking about June, July, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He was there. But makes a difference based on evidence that has been presented to this Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it was or not in those moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of course, where in those months. Yes, absolutely that was the point of my objection as opposed to what Mr. Hedaraly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you ask further details, Mr. Kehoe, in cross-examination if you think that the matter is not dealt with in such a way that it is sufficiently assists the Chamber, but there is no reason at that moment to object against that question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President I would like to be heard on this score when we do have a break.
