utterances.text: Yes, please. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Speaking of breaks, Your Honour, I don't know what the Chamber had in mind. I know there was a break before the witness started. But I don't know if that's a formal break or not, so I would seek the Court's guidance in terms of timing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were invited to rephrase the question in a more neutral way, such as did you ever learn about whether the production was -- had been the same always or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. I was asking about breaks in the -- in the session since we had a long break, but not really -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's the guidance I was seeking. But thank you for the guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break and we'll start at ten minutes to 1.00 and have a break until ten minutes past 1.00. Not now, Madam Usher. I wouldn't say comedy of errors but it seems that -- Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And let me ask you the question in the way that the Presiding Judge has suggested. Did you ever learn whether the production in the Tvik factory would be changed to anything other than nuts and bolts?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: No. And -- and on tours through the factory, we saw no evidence of any production at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, were you able to observe the machinery that was used in the -- in the Tvik factory?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The manager took us on tours through the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether this machinery could be used to produce anything other than nuts and bolts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, there is no foundation for that question, whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you have any now, is the foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as, I could see, it was a very old-fashioned production facility that could not easily be used for any more fancy production.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you have any experience in relation to machinery and products that can be produced by machinery, or is it just a layman's impression.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be a layman's impression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, did you hear about the negotiations between the RSK and the government of Croatia on 3 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Affirmative. We knew about the -- the starting up of the peace talks in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you have any further knowledge on those talks about those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: We had no detailed information about -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time since the witness doesn't have any knowledge, I'd like to bar table 65 ter 3991, which is at line 48 of the spreadsheet, but the number of the document, 65 ter 3996, which is number 49, and 65 ter 4115, which is item 353. They all talk about these negotiations -- there is already evidence before there Court about them and these are ECMM reports about those negotiations. There's no need to go with the witness through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against bar table admission of 3991, 3996, and 4115.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'd like to take a look at them to follow the bar table procedure that the Chamber has established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is just a brief description and what to specifically look at, that's -- have you prepared that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Not in written form, but we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do it in such a way, and we'll provisionally MFI them so that once the Defence has seen the proper document to introduce them that we can hear from them. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these will become Exhibit P1295 through P1297 respectively, all marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to move to the next page of your first statement, P1283. And you state --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps this could be a good time for a break. I'm going change topics. So if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, we'll have a break now. We'll then resume at ten minutes past 1.00, sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, where the Chamber would have given you later this morning, an opportunity to further make further submissions in relation to your objection. I now understand that you will deal with the matter on cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, moving to the page of the statement on the screen that is the next page in your hard copy, page number 3, at the top, you say: "From my position, I could see impacts all over the city and especially the area in the immediate vicinity of the hospital. Houses close to mine were hit, and heavy smoke generated from a residential area only a few hundred metres to the south." And then a little later on: "One grenade impacted only 20 metres from our HQ." Mr. Hansen, can you clarify for the Court when you made these observations?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That was in the early hours of the morning of the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And where were you specifically when you made these observations?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: I was at our office, at the ECMM headquarters in -- close to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can have what has been marked for identification as P1293.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that's the aerial photo of Knin that you marked. And while that comes up, let me ask you about the next portion of that paragraph, when you say: "In the afternoon en route to UN HQ, we passed the above mentioned areas, pure residential, and saw private houses still ablaze, among them also the residence of the Orthodox priest. We passed Tvik and saw the impact, proceeded to the main street and passed impacts in the middle of the street." Now what I'd like to you do is, with the assistance of the usher, if can you mark for us the location of the house of the Orthodox priest that you saw being hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we can move to a different portion of the -- of the photo. We'll get to that later on. If we can zoom back out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. What is circled here is the ECMM headquarters --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That what's you refer to as number 1, Roman numeral I.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That's true. And the house of the Orthodox priest is one - sorry - these houses here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you circle where you think that house is?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: One of these here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And could you put an A next to that.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now when you were allowed out of the UN camp on 7th August, on your first trip to Knin, and we'll talk about that trip in more detail, but did you see this house again?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: On the 7th, when we saw -- honestly, I'm -- I'm not totally sure on that if it was the 7th or the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you see that house again after you were allowed to leave the camp, either on the 7th or later?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That's true, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how did that house look?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Well, at that time it was a ruin. It was burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have P1293 with the marking admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P1298.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now later in that same statement in the paragraph right before number 4, you talk about your patrols on the 6th to the 8th, and that you could see impacts in the streets near the residential areas. And I just want to -- while the picture is on the screen, those the areas that you identified as III Roman numeral; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you also circled the hospital as 3. Now, to your knowledge, was the hospital hit by shells?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: To my knowledge, there was no structural damage, and therefore not a direct hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you see shells in the area of the hospital, impacting in the area of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we saw, in the general area of the hospital, we saw impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in that same paragraph you state: "The shelling is assessed to be psychological, with the purpose to drive out the Serb population. The shelling was not meant to destroy the city, and the general idea of the attack seems to be the retaking of an intact and population-wise empty city." Now, Mr. Hansen, can you provide the Trial Chamber because this conclusion itself is not of assistance to the Chamber, can you provide the Chamber with the facts ans observations that formed the basis of that assessment?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, during the first day of the shelling, we could hear certainly the impact throughout town and we could see smoke develop in different quarters of the town. We had the hospital area in direct line of sights and could see the impact there and certainly we saw the impact that landed just in our own garden. At the time we -- we could patrol. I went to town and to the residential area close to the Tvik factory, and what we saw there was impact -- I would call it somehow, occasional impact with no structural damage; and we saw basically facades on high-rise buildings being -- bear witness of shrapnels and -- so the conclusion is that we did not see any targeted structural damage, more a -- an occasional shelling of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when later in the statement you said that what you believed to be military targets were not targeted, do I take -- should I take that to mean there was no damage to them?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is true. We -- I did not go into the northern barracks, but passing by, we did not see any structural damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can have Exhibit P1292 marked for identification. That is your diary. That is at tab 21 of your binder. And you have the original Danish as well in the binder if you want to refer to that. I will refer to the English, for obvious reasons. And if we can go to page 2 when it comes up on the screen. In the middle of that paragraph, that is one of your entries for the 4th of August, you say in the middle of that paragraph: "I can quite simply not accept how people are being driven out. I can understand the Croats, but I'm really disgusted by their methods. They are breaking all the laws of war." Now, Mr. Hansen, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Well, it's again referring to the nature of the shelling. It appeared at this point it was targeting the -- driving out of the population of Knin rather than anything else, and -- so at this point in time, we concluded that the operation had the objective to re-take the geography of the RSK rather than -- with an empty population.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me now show you 65 ter 4026, which is on tab 50 of your binder. And just for the Court's information, the tabs are matching the exhibit list so when we come to admission, it may be easier. If you refer to that document. This is a special report from the chief for logistics of ECMM whose name is redacted. But let me just ask you: Do you know who that was on 4 August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: I recall him as -- you mean the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was he with you in the ECMM shelter on 4 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Correct, yes he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now regarding the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And this was the only time that that -- that a redacted name will be disclosed in my examination just so that all the parties will rest assured. I noticed Mr. Kehoe's microphone is still on. I don't know if he was planning on saying something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, let's get back to the report. And the author of this report says -- well, without mentioning the name, was the author of this report with you in the ECMM shelter on 4 August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: He was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And he says, regarding the 4th of August: "Shelling Knin started at 500 hours. ECMM team took cover in the shelter during the day. Fifty refugees from the neighbourhood joined ECMM building, most of them families of our accomodation." Now, Mr. Hansen, do you recall neighbourhood families seeking shelter to the ECMM headquarters on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And I knew quite a lot of -- of the persons taking shelter in our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court whether these were civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: They were all civilian, mostly elders, women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you talk to the Court, what was the atmosphere in the ECMM shelter?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Well, there was an atmosphere of uncertainty, nervousness, and people afraid, scared, children crying, and absolutely uncertainty. Nobody knew anything about what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to have 65 ter 4026 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, let me change topics now and talk a little bit about the looting that you witnessed. First I want to start when you were still in the UN camp, not allowed to get out, as described in your statement. Actually, why don't I deal with that briefly first. If you go to tab 25 of your binder. That is 65 ter 7008. There is a report from the 7th of August, covering the period 4 to 6 August. On the third page of this report, under political situation, it says: "ECMM in Knin are blocked in their barracks by five HV tanks and are not allowed to patrol the town nor investigate reports of small-arms shooting. May suggest that clean-up operation that they did not want the UN to witness." Mr. Hansen, do you remember being prevented from leaving the UN camp by five HV tanks?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: While we're on this document right after it says: "ECMM reports that there are strong indications of killings of ARSK soldiers following the taking of Knin and states that the town had on 6 August been cleared of dead bodies on 5 August." Next paragraph : "ECMM ... reports on 6 August that in some parts of the former RSK territory advancing HV units burnt and destroyed livestock and property, abandoned by Krajina Serbs ..." My question for you is, can you tell the Court what was the source of this information that ARSK soldiers were being killed and that advancing HV units burned and destroyed livestock and property?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Mostly I would say that it is an anecdotal information given to us by refugees. At this point by residents from Knin and the surrounding areas seeking refuge in the southern barracks where we were hosted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, if I could have 65 ter 7008 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to correct the record on something, Your Honour. Page 74, line 11 what appears to have been read in was that ECMM reports. I've lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: ECMM in Knin. Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It says actually, UN forces are blocked in the barracks, not ECMM are blocked in their barracks. The report itself says, UN forces are blocked in their barracks by five HV tanks not that ECMM forces are blocked. That's the correction I wanted to make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't think that is it right, but the document is in evidence. Can we have 65 ter 7008 admitted into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Then, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I hate to rise again, Your Honour, but this -- it may be a minor point, but we have all made mistakes reading documents into the record. If you look at the page under political situation, it says something crossed out and then later on in that same line it says, "UN forces are blocked in their barracks." Now in the transcript, it doesn't say that. It wasn't read that way and that's the only thing I was trying to point out was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now let's see, where exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's page 73, line 24. I was looking at 74, line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was focussing on the source Mr. Hedaraly gave and I had difficulties in finding it. Mr. Hedaraly, the correction you would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question to you, Mr. Hansen. Could you tell me exactly what you mean by anecdotal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would talk to -- to the persons who were seeking shelter in the barracks, and I would categorise the information as anecdotal, as people were under no obligation to reveal a -- a fact to us or -- I believe we had no means of verifying the information at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just what people told you, not in a systematic questioning of those persons but just what -- what they spontaneously uttered to say so. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that is true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I have another question and that relates to something you said before the break. You said, "We saw no production," when you were talking about the Tvik factory. Now, production, from what I understand, can mean a lot of things but among others the following: Production, the act of producing something but also the result of that act, that is a product. Now did you want to say that you didn't see any production ongoing or did you intend to say that you did not see any products.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Happy to clarify that, Your Honour. We saw a lot of boxes and pallets with nuts and bolts but did not see any operating machinery. So no ongoing production, but previous production.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, I want to go back to your first statement, at tab 1 which is P1283; and I want to focus again on page 3 of that statement, in the second paragraph, in the middle you say: "Shortly after" -- and you're referring about when the Croatian flag was flying over Knin castle: "Shortly after, we saw all means of remaining Serb vehicles, i.e., vans, cars, tractors, bikes, used by HV 4th Brigade to collect valuables from the left-behind apartments and houses in front of the UN HQ. A big garage was used as a storage site." Then you say: "A great number of vehicles off-loaded the goods at this storage site guarded by the HV troops. The 6th August evening and night, it was all loaded on military trucks and carried away, direction Drnis." And, Mr. Hansen, can you tell the Court exactly what you saw?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. As -- we were, as I said before, we were prevented from leaving the barracks but we could go to the top of buildings. And just outside the perimeter, we saw an appeared to a parking area for lorries or trucks, and that particular site was used for the compilation of commodities that you were brought in by uniformed personnel. It was -- we also saw that a particular building was used as a storage, and it appeared it was a garage. So what we saw, the activities that was ongoing, more or less, throughout the day was that all kinds of vehicles were used to transport commodities and then further on, they were unloaded on trucks and taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you the aerial photo again, P62, a blank aerial photo and we will ask to focus on the UN camp on that photo. While that photo loads up because it's pretty large, let me ask you: You talked about commodities. What type of commodities did you see brought there on the 5th and then taken away on the 6th?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: We saw television sets, stereos, refrigerators, and this kind of stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And while we're still waiting let me ask you, you identify the HV 4th Brigade collecting these items. How did you know that they were HV 4th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the -- the insignia was painted on -- on some of the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen. Once that picture comes up, I will ask you to identify the garage where you saw these HV 4th Brigade soldiers collecting valuables on the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to focus on the UN camp, at the bottom right. Maybe just zoom in a little more. Thank you. And if we can have the assistance of the usher to help the witness mark the location of that garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you can circle it, and place an A next to it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we have this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit P1301 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen. I now want to move to the 7th and 8th of August, the first days after you were allowed to leave the UN compound. I will refer to both your diary and your third statement. I will start with your diary, which is P1292, which is tab 21 of your binder, and the entry for the 7th of August, which is page 5. At the beginning where you say: "I went into Knin twice today. Knin is no longer Knin. The main road through the town has been destroyed. Large craters and shop windows have been blown out. Houses, either are or have been in flames. The objective of the first tour was to fetch our things from HQ ... where we lived. We were just in time to save the computers and communications equipment. The Croats were already in action when we got there. We told them it was ECMM property, and they left with nothing more than a little bit of diesel." Mr. Hansen, do you remember seeing Croatian soldiers at the ECMM headquarters when you arrived there on the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And who was with you on that first trip?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: ECMM colleagues were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you identify those?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: By name?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, one colleague was which I am very sure was there, was Soren Liborius, and as far as I remember also Mr. Eric Hendriks participated in this trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen. And after going to the ECMM headquarters you went to your own accommodation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you also recount that in your diary when you say: "My own lodgings had also visitors. Everything was upside down but luckily my civilian clothes and uniform was still there. My camera, CD's, speakers, et cetera, were gone." If we could just leave the diary on the screen for a while, you refer to your third statement at tab 3, at paragraph 20; and there you say about the same trip: "My interpreter's house is located in the residential area, north of the Tvik factory and the house had shrapnel on the its walls and was damaged because of the shell impacts, although the house did not receive a direct hit. The house was also missing a number of valuable items, such as a TV set. The main entrance door was broken, and the house had been completely ransacked." And I wanted to go on to the next page on your diary, I'll ask my question: "In the first few days after the attack it seemed that a certain discipline prevailed, but now I can see that every single houses has been gone through with a tooth comb and all valuables removed." Mr. Hansen, can you explain to the Court what was the basis of that statement?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. We as I said, in the -- in the diary entry, we met people who were removing stuff from -- from our office and our private houses when we got there. But also further on driving through town, it was obvious that -- that each and every single house was broken into or every apartment was broken into, and -- and we saw -- it was at this point very visible in -- in -- in the streets that the people were collecting items.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I saw the clock, Mr. President. We can adjourn here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one issue with the -- with the witness here. If we could have the opportunity to just take a look at the witness's original diary not the Xerox copy, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you would like to see the original rather than --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, do you have your diary, the original with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have it with me here, but I have it in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you be willing to -- to leave it the hands of the Defence for, just for verifying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very briefly. How much time would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, the Defence can make that request of Prosecution. We asked the witness, and the witness provided photocopies of the portions that were -- that were here now -- to we -- wants the original diary. They have -- they can compare the handwritten photocopies with what has been provided in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that, and I think it's in general to see the original is a reasonable wish. You would be willing to give it temporarily, and the Defence will return it to you, to Mr. Kehoe and his colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, can I bring it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or would it be -- if you say. I dont' know what exactly you are having for --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We an take a look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the issue is that if something strikes your eyes tomorrow and then there is not sufficient time then rather have it done this afternoon but then through the victims and witness section that it could be delivered and that you return it within say, one hour, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other Defence teams interested in looking at the original? Mr. Kuzmanovic, you now then stay close to Mr. Kehoe. I take it you'll find a way to -- So if you could please provide to the victims and witness section the original, and the professional obligation of Defence counsel is to return it to you in exactly the same state as they received it. We'll then adjourn and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry Mr. President. Didn't instruct the witness not to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. And I highly appreciate that not only Mr. Misetic assisting me in keeping the speed of speech such that everyone can follow, but thank you very much. Mr. Hansen, you are instructed that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether the testimony you gave today or the testimony still to be given. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
